set.descent_text: The route ends on the back slopes of Temple Crag, and the summit is a short hike from the top if time allows. The way down is the standard Contact Pass descent: follow the back slopes to steep rock where a short rappel off fixed slings reaches Contact Pass. Below the pass, snow or loose scree and talus lead back to the lakes. Early in the season the snow below the pass can be kicked down or glissaded, but the scree and talus are loose and tiring.
set.approach: Start at the Glacier Lodge trailhead at the end of Crocker Street west of Big Pine, and follow the North Fork of Big Pine Creek trail past First Lake. Leave the trail near Second Lake, where most parties camp, and cross to the foot of the crag by scree slopes or the snowfield. From the base of the climb, traverse a ledge leftward to the buttress and scramble up a few hundred feet until the rock steepens; this is where the rope goes on. A good option is a snow chute running up the wall that lies between the Sun Ribbon and Moon Goddess aretes; crampons are useful early in the season.

review.notes: MP Moon Goddess: scramble from ledge traverse, rope up where steeper; descent back slopes to steep rocks (rappel) to Contact Pass then snow/scree. MP Contact Pass Crack: standard descent for the north-face aretes, rappel from fixed nut/piton. MP Venusian: shared start via snowfield. MP area page + Burd report: trailhead, Second Lake. SummitPost not readable by script so not listed.

set.descent_text: From the top of the arete, descend east on a climbers' trail toward Contact Pass. The trail turns into class 3 above the pass and then steepens to class 4 and 5 terrain, where most parties rappel from slings to the pass. Below the pass, snow can be glissaded and rock and scree lead back to the lakes. A rappel station on the left side of the arete higher up allows a short rappel into the gully, from which class 3 and 4 climbing reaches the summit plateau.
set.approach: Start at the Glacier Lodge trailhead at the end of Crocker Street west of Big Pine, and follow the North Fork of Big Pine Creek trail past First Lake. Leave the trail near Second Lake and climb toward the base of the crag. Venusian Blind shares its start with Moon Goddess Arete: a snow chute between the Sun Ribbon and Moon Goddess aretes leads to a snow and rock traverse to the base. The snowfield is steep enough that crampons suit early season. Roughly 300 feet of third and fourth class leads to ledges, where Moon Goddess splits right and Venusian goes left; a short right-facing corner marks the start.

review.notes: MP Venusian Blind page gives descent and approach. Contact Pass Crack and Moon Goddess pages agree on Contact Pass as the descent with a rappel. Rap length left out.

set.descent_text: The usual way down is through Contact Pass, which is unpleasant however you reach it. Reach the pass and rappel once, on a single rope, from the station furthest right, which puts you on scree; then slog back down to the snowfield and your camp, or to the trail and the car. Start early, as the descent needs attention and the crag is exposed to electrical storms. A way to avoid the pass is to traverse along the crest toward Gayley and Sill instead.
set.approach: Start at the Glacier Lodge trailhead at the end of Crocker Street west of Big Pine, and follow the North Fork of Big Pine Creek trail past First Lake. Second Lake is the usual camp. In the afternoon, climb to the base of the route in soft snow, which hardens by morning; light aluminum crampons help on a car-to-car day early in the season. The common start is a crack in a left-facing dihedral beside a large grey scar, well above the foot of the Dark Star buttress.

review.notes: MP Sun Ribbon page: descent via Contact Pass with single-rope rappel from rightmost station; start near grey scar; camp at Second Lake. Contact Pass Crack confirms the pass as the standard descent.

set.descent_text: From the top of the crag, work down the gully for a long way, staying high and heading straight down before it steepens sharply and drops to the right. Ledges and steps lead to an obvious rappel off blocks at the very top of Contact Pass. A different gully has anchors but lands well below the pass, so you climb sand back up to it. At the pass itself, expect loose blocks, sand and difficult route finding.
set.approach: Start at the Glacier Lodge trailhead at the end of Crocker Street west of Big Pine, and follow the North Fork of Big Pine Creek trail past First Lake. Leave the trail near Second Lake or Third Lake and head to the toe of the north face. The route starts at the lowest point of the face, marked by a burst of white crystals, where lower fifth class climbing leads up; others hike around the buttress's left flank and cross back right along a broad ledge. A bivouac below the crag is a common way to get an early start.

review.notes: MP Dark Star: descent gully to top of Contact Pass, alt gully with anchors; start at lowest point or around left and traverse right on ledge. MP Barefoot Bynum: Dark Star start is a burst of white crystals. MP area: bivouacs beneath the crag. Contact Pass Crack: rappel at the pass.

set.approach: Start at the Glacier Lodge trailhead at the end of Crocker Street west of Big Pine, and follow the North Fork of Big Pine Creek trail past First Lake. Continue to Third Lake, then cross the outlet stream on fallen logs at the east end of the lake and follow a use trail onto the moraine. The trail fades after a short distance, and the rest of the way is talus and scree heading roughly south. Head for the wall under the route's shallow dihedral, which lies right of the Barefoot Bynum and Dark Star starts.

review.notes: MP Planaria location gives the Third Lake approach. Descent skipped: the page says the first ascent party ended at the top of the lower buttress while the free ascent went to the summit, so the top-out is not fixed.

set.approach: Start at the Glacier Lodge trailhead at the end of Crocker Street west of Big Pine, and follow the North Fork of Big Pine Creek trail past First Lake. Leave the trail near Second Lake or Third Lake and head up the scree and talus to the north face. The route starts about forty feet right of the start of Dark Star, which is marked by a burst of white crystals, and follows a right-facing dihedral. It joins Dark Star at the top of the lower buttress.

review.notes: MP Barefoot Bynum: start 40 ft right of Dark Star, joins Dark Star atop lower buttress. Descent skipped: the stored line is unsourced and no readable page states the descent from the lower buttress.

set.approach: Start at the Glacier Lodge trailhead at the end of Crocker Street west of Big Pine, and follow the North Fork of Big Pine Creek trail past First Lake. Leave the trail near Second Lake and climb to the foot of the crag. Eclipsed Arete is the arete furthest left on the northeast face, beside Venusian Blind, and the approach is mostly the same: a snow chute and a traverse to the base of Venusian Blind, then a traverse left toward the arete. Early-season snow may call for crampons.

review.notes: MP Eclipsed Arete: left-most arete, approach mostly same as Venusian Blind; Venusian page gives the snow chute. Descent skipped: the narrative never says where it tops out or how the party descended.

set.descent_text: The traverse ends on Mount Sill. From its summit, descend the third-class ridge in the direction of Polemonium, then drop into the L-shaped couloir and Glacier Notch to reach the Palisade Glacier. The starts of both are not obvious, but cairns usually mark them. From the glacier, you can either go straight down to Second or Third Lake, which is more direct and best with snow, or follow the trail past Sam Mack Meadow to rejoin the North Fork of Big Pine Creek trail.
set.approach: Start at the Glacier Lodge trailhead at the end of Crocker Street west of Big Pine, and follow the North Fork of Big Pine Creek trail past First Lake. There are two main places to cross the creek: on the east shore of Second Lake (reached between First and Second Lakes) and at the Third Lake outlet. The first is more reliable when water is high. The spots to leave the main trail are well used. After crossing, walk off-trail up to the foot of Temple Crag.

review.notes: Single MP traverse page for the descent and creek crossings; MP area page for trailhead. No distances given because the two pages disagree on the distance to Second Lake.

set.approach: Start at the Glacier Lodge trailhead at the end of Crocker Street west of Big Pine, and follow the North Fork of Big Pine Creek trail past First Lake. Leave the trail near Second Lake or Third Lake and go to the foot of the crag. The couloir is the first chute left of the Dark Star buttresses on the northeast face; it holds steep snow low down and is typically climbed in late May or early June.

review.notes: MP Mendenhall page: location (first chute left of Dark Star buttresses), best season, steep snow low. Descent skipped: the page does not describe it.

set.approach: Start at the Glacier Lodge trailhead at the end of Crocker Street west of Big Pine, and follow the North Fork of Big Pine Creek trail past First Lake. Continue to Third Lake and go toward the north face of Temple Crag. Once below it, head south and climb a long talus slope to the notch on the east side of the crag, which is Contact Pass. Cross the pass and descend to the south face, a wide face with slabs and tarns; the route is a crack and chimney line near the right edge, left of a small tower on the skyline.

review.notes: MP Backside of Beyond location + the AAJ 1999 text on the page for the line. Descent skipped: the page does not state it.
